ARCH 01

Mathematical Zero-Access & Inherent Non-Custody

When Coralgenz Global invented the proprietary .secure format, our core engineering directive was to remove trust from the privacy equation. In conventional cloud storage (Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive), the vendor manages the decryption keys on server clusters, meaning employees, rogue actors, or government warrants can read your plaintext documents.

Coralgenz Vault operates on a Zero-Knowledge Architecture. All cryptographic key derivation, envelope assembly, file encryption, and payload decryption execute strictly within your client device's browser runtime via the W3C Web Cryptography API (SubtleCrypto).

// Client-side non-custody invariant:
Server_State(User_Payload) = Ciphertext_Blob_AES256GCM
Server_State(Master_Key) = NULL (Never generated, received, or transmitted)
Decryption_Capacity(Coralgenz_Global) = IMPOSSIBLE [0% probability]

Even in the event of an infrastructure breach, hostile server takeover, or physical seizure of our cloud database disks, an attacker receives only ciphertext indistinguishable from pure cryptographic noise.

ARCH 02

Dual-Stage Cryptographic Derivation Pipeline

To prevent GPU-accelerated dictionary attacks, rainbow table matching, and quantum-adjacent brute force, Coralgenz Vault implements a proprietary 4-stage cryptographic pipeline:

Client-Side Cryptographic Workflow (Inside Browser RAM)
STEP 01 Master Password User Input (RAM)
STEP 02 HMAC-SHA-512 MILSPEC_PEPPER_V6
STEP 03 2,000,000 PBKDF2 Unique Base64 Salt
STEP 04 AES-256-GCM Authenticated 256-bit
STEP 05 Integrity Check SHA-256 Hash Match
  • Dual-Stage Pre-Hashing: The user's master password is pre-hashed using HMAC-SHA-512 combined with a dynamic client-assembled pepper string (e.g. MILSPEC_PEPPER_V6). This pre-hash neutralizes length-extension exploits and prevents direct password exposure.
  • 2,000,000 PBKDF2 Iterations: The pre-hashed secret is fed into PBKDF2 with SHA-256 executing an unprecedented 2,000,000 computation rounds against a cryptographically random salt (generated via crypto.getRandomValues()).
  • AES-256-GCM Authenticated Cipher: Galois/Counter Mode (GCM) guarantees both mathematical confidentiality and payload authenticity. Any byte tampering automatically fails authentication prior to decryption.
  • Cryptographic Tamper Alert (INTEGRITY_HASH): Following decryption, the resulting byte array is verified against a hardcoded SHA-256 digest to prove that zero silent corruption or MITM modification occurred.
ARCH 03

What Coralgenz Sees vs. What You See

Under our zero-knowledge paradigm, there is a total separation between what your authenticated browser displays and what our backend database stores:

Data Element What Coralgenz Servers Store & See What You See in Your Browser
Master Password NOTHING (0 Bytes stored or transmitted) Password entered in your local browser input field
Derived Decryption Key NOTHING (Key never touches network) Ephemeral CryptoKey object in client volatile RAM
File Name & Extension Obfuscated random container ID (e.g., vlt_89f7a1c.secure) Actual file name (e.g., file_example_XLS_10.xls.secure)
File Contents & Payload Ciphertext Noise (AES-256-GCM encrypted byte stream) Decrypted spreadsheet, PDF, source code, or media
File Metadata & Attributes Encrypted container metadata block Original creation dates, MIME types, file size
ARCH 04

Volatile Memory Zeroization (zeroizeMemory) Protocol

Traditional web applications leave decrypted files floating in the browser's JavaScript heap, rendering them vulnerable to memory dump tools, cold-boot extractions, or compromised extensions.

Coralgenz Vault implements an active zeroizeMemory() anti-forensics protocol that aggressively purges sensitive bytes from volatile RAM:

function zeroizeMemory() {
  if (decryptedBuffer) decryptedBuffer.fill(0); // Actively overwrite RAM with zeroes
  if (activeBlobUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(activeBlobUrl); // Revoke memory pointers
  document.getElementById('vault-viewer').innerHTML = ''; // Clean DOM nodes
  sessionStorage.clear(); // Purge ephemeral cache
}
  • Immediate Buffer Overwriting: As soon as a file is locked or closed, the decrypted Uint8Array buffer is explicitly wiped using .fill(0) before garbage collection triggers.
  • Automated Lifecycle Traps: zeroizeMemory() executes unconditionally upon window.onbeforeunload, window.onpagehide, visibilitychange (hidden), and idle session expiration.
  • Screen Guard & DLP Defense: When the browser window loses focus or a screenshot command is detected, the container instantly obscures the viewport to thwart unauthorized capture.
ARCH 05

Legal Inquiries, Subpoenas & Government Warrants

As an Indian corporation headquartered in Coimbatore, Coralgenz Global strictly complies with all lawful statutory orders, subpoenas, and court mandates issued by competent jurisdictions.

The Mathematics of Subpoena Compliance

If Coralgenz Global is served with a court subpoena, search warrant, or government disclosure order commanding the release of a user's unencrypted files or decryption keys: we cannot comply because we do not possess the keys.

Our zero-knowledge architecture is purposefully designed so that no administrative backdoor, master override key, or server-side key escrow exists anywhere in our organization. In response to valid legal process, we can only provide the encrypted ciphertext blobs we store, which cannot be decrypted without the user's master password.

ARCH 06

Shared Responsibility Model for Zero-Knowledge Vaults

True zero-knowledge encryption requires a shared understanding of security custody between the infrastructure provider and the user:

Coralgenz Global Responsibility Your Sole Responsibility
Maintaining mathematical integrity of the AES-256-GCM WebCrypto engine Selecting a strong, high-entropy Master Password
Executing 2,000,000 PBKDF2 iterations with unique salt per container Safeguarding your Master Password (No password reset is possible if lost)
Automated volatile memory zeroization (zeroizeMemory) on window blur Ensuring your physical device is free of malware, keyloggers, or malicious extensions
99.99% cloud storage uptime and tamper-evident ciphertext backups Maintaining offline container backups for mission-critical archives

CRITICAL WARNING: Because Coralgenz Global never stores your password, there is NO "Forgot Password" feature. If you forget your password, your encrypted .secure files CANNOT be recovered by our engineers.

ARCH 07

Telemetry, Analytics & Zero-Logging Invariant

We uphold an uncompromising zero-telemetry policy for all files processed through Coralgenz Vault:

  • Zero Content Telemetry: We do not scan, parse, OCR, index, analyze, or fingerprint any file uploaded or unlocked in Coralgenz Vault.
  • Zero AI Model Training: Your files are never utilized for training machine learning or generative AI algorithms.
  • Zero Third-Party Pixels: The Coralgenz Vault application environment has a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) of default-src 'none', prohibiting external trackers, analytics beacons, or third-party ad networks.
  • Minimal Account Telemetry: Account-level data is limited to email address (for account authentication), storage quota utilized (in bytes), and subscription status.
ARCH 08

Statutory Alignment (DPDP Act 2023 & EU GDPR)

Zero-knowledge encryption represents the gold standard of "Privacy by Design and by Default" mandated under Article 25 of the GDPR and Section 8(5) of India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023:

  • Reasonable Security Safeguards: Section 8(5) of the DPDP Act 2023 requires Data Fiduciaries to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches. Client-side AES-256-GCM encryption with 2,000,000 PBKDF2 iterations constitutes the most robust technical safeguard achievable in modern computing.
  • Data Portability: Standalone .secure files are self-contained HTML/cryptographic packages. You can download and decrypt them completely offline in any web browser without needing our servers.
  • Right to Erasure: When you delete an encrypted container from Coralgenz Vault, the ciphertext blob is immediately wiped from our active databases and purged from backup rotations.
ARCH 09

Frequently Asked Architecture Questions

Who invented the .secure file format?
The .secure file format was invented by Coralgenz Global, an enterprise cryptographic technology company in Coimbatore, India. It was created as the world's first browser-native zero-knowledge encrypted container capable of decrypting files entirely in offline browser memory.
Can Coralgenz engineers recover my files if I lose my password?
No. Because Coralgenz Vault employs true zero-knowledge encryption, there is no master key, recovery escrow, or backdoor. If your master password is lost, the file remains permanently encrypted ciphertext that cannot be decrypted by anyone.
How can I audit or report a cryptographic security vulnerability?
We welcome independent security audits and coordinated vulnerability disclosures. Security researchers can email our Cryptographic Response Team directly at security@coralgenz.co.in or contact@coralgenz.co.in with PGP-encrypted details. We respond to verified reports within 24 hours.
